# Psalm 36 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. Of-the-servant of-YHWH, of-David.

**2** An-oracle of-transgression to-the-wicked [is] within my-heart: there-is-no dread of-God before his-eyes.

**3** For it-flatters-him in-his-eyes, to-find his-iniquity, to-hate.

**4** The-words of-his-mouth [are] iniquity and-deceit; he-has-ceased to-act-wisely, to-do-good.

**5** Iniquity he-devises on-his-bed; he-sets-himself on-a-way not good; evil he-does-not reject.

**6** YHWH, in-the-heavens [is] Your-steadfast-love; Your-faithfulness [reaches] to-the-clouds.

**7** Your-righteousness [is] like-the-mountains of-God; Your-judgments [are] a-great deep. Man and-beast You-save, YHWH.

**8** How-precious [is] Your-steadfast-love, O-God! And-the-sons of-man in-the-shadow of-Your-wings take-refuge.

**9** They-feast on-the-abundance of-Your-house, and-the-river of-Your-delights You-give-them-to-drink.

**10** For with-You [is] the-fountain of-life; in-Your-light we-see light.

**11** Extend Your-steadfast-love to-those-who-know-You, and-Your-righteousness to-the-upright of-heart.

**12** Let-not come to-me the-foot of-pride, and-the-hand of-the-wicked — let-it-not drive-me-away.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **36:10**: 'Fountain of life' and 'light' — two of the most profound theological metaphors in the Psalter combined in one verse.

— EMET
